items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: I'd already been to an agent's office who was Eddie Elkort

ctx.x: I did a number for him and man, I can't begin to tell you that I couldn't take the job. They wanted to give me 20 pounds, I think it was -- 20 pounds -- 20 marks, that's $5.00 -- isn't that right? Four marks is a dollar -- anyway, I think it was 20 marks a performance or 20 marks a show -- something like that. Anyhow, I couldn't take it and I didn't have no money in my pocket at all.

Now, don't forget, I'd already been to an agent's office who was Eddie Elkort--- I forget this guy's name, the agent. Anyhow I went to his office and the girl told me how much they pay for me, I told them I was from America, showed them my pictures and everything how long I did work, how much time I do on the stage and all and she says, the best thing we pay is $15 a show, I think. I says, 'Yeah?'

This is for special service now, this is. That's all the agents were booking over there, special service. That's what this was and that's what this guy, Lee Bouveau was booking, Special Service. However, I said no. So I showed them my pictures. Somebody got on the phone and I'm ready to go now, so when she got on the phone I'm ready to go. So she hollered to and says, "Don't you want to leave one of your pictures?" And to me I just said, just another picture left, that's all. I'll just give her another picture,…
